name: Nadir Oceanus
specific_features: Uncharted deep-ocean structures of unknown origin
description: Nadir Oceanus earns its name from the staggering depth of its global ocean, which plunges over forty-five kilometers at its deepest measured point. The immense pressure at the seabed compresses water into exotic ice phases that form a solid layer atop the rocky mantle. Above this ice floor, hydrothermal vent megaclusters pump superheated mineral-rich water into the deep, creating oases of warmth in an otherwise lightless abyss.

The dense atmosphere weighs on the ocean surface with tangible force, and the air itself feels thick in the lungs. Storms on Nadir Oceanus are rare but catastrophic, generating waves that can reach a hundred meters in height before the atmospheric pressure dampens them. The surface waters are deceptively calm most of the time, a dark mirror reflecting the heavy grey sky.

Deep-scan surveys have detected geometric structures on the pressure-ice seabed, too regular to be natural but at depths no probe has survived to photograph. Their composition appears to be a material distinct from the surrounding ice, possibly metallic, but the crushing pressure destroys instruments before they can complete analysis. No civilization has been detected on or near the planet, raising the question of who or what built at the bottom of an alien sea.

Nadir Oceanus presents one of the most tantalizing mysteries in explored space, but the engineering challenges of deep investigation are currently insurmountable. Platinum deposits concentrated around the hydrothermal vents are accessible to mid-depth mining operations, providing economic justification for continued orbital presence. Every expedition that arrives adds new sonar data to the map of the seabed structures, slowly assembling a picture that no one yet understands.
